summary: Spurs lined up in a 4-2-3-1 against Aston Villa's 4-2-3-1 (9 changes from the Liverpool game).
Spurs created the better chances (1.56 xG to 1.16) and deserved more than a defeat.
Compared with their other league games, Spurs played higher up the pitch (75% vs 63%), pressed harder (3.3 vs 4.8), conceded less (1.16 xG vs 1.48 xG), went long less often (3.0% vs 3.6%).
Van Hecke was the biggest attacking threat (0.65 xG + xA); Bentancur won the ball back most often (8 tackles won + interceptions).

phases.title: Build-up and possession

rows.label: Long balls, share of accurate passes

read: Spurs had 64% of the ball (season average 58%), completing 504 of 581 passes (87%).
75% of all passing in the opposition half was by Spurs (field tilt), above their usual 63%. They spent long spells camped in Aston Villa's half.
39% of Spurs' accurate passes were in their own half (195 own half, 309 opposition half): most of the passing happened high up the pitch.
Long balls made up 3.0% of accurate passes (in line with the season's 3.6%), with 44% of long balls finding a teammate. Spurs built short and rarely went direct.

phases.title: Chance creation
read: 20 shots (7 on target) worth 1.56 xG, 0.08 per shot; the season average is 0.08 per shot, so the chances were of typical quality.
12 shots came from inside the box and 8 from outside (40% from distance).
Spurs created 4 big chances and missed 2 (season average 2.2).
31 touches in Aston Villa's box, in line with the season average of 30; Aston Villa had 19 in Spurs' box.
Where the xG came from: open play 0.67 (54%), fast breaks 0.00, set pieces 0.57. 8 of the shots came straight from a teammate's pass (assisted).
13 successful take-ons (68% success), season average 11.4.

phases.title: Finishing
read: Spurs scored 2 from 1.56 xG: 0.4 more than the chances were worth.
Shots on target were worth 2.32 xGOT against 1.56 xG before the shot: the finishing placed shots better than average.
Aston Villa's goalkeeper made 5 saves.

phases.title: Out of possession
read: PPDA (estimated): 3.3 Aston Villa passes in their own half per Spurs defensive action; season average 4.8. Lower means a more aggressive press, so this was a more intense press than usual.
35 tackles won and 10 interceptions (season averages 15.0 and 7.8); 9 clearances and 3 blocks.
Duels: Spurs won 65, Aston Villa 46 (59% for Spurs); 45% of aerial duels won.
Aston Villa managed 15 shots worth 1.16 xG (Spurs usually concede 1.48 xG) and 2 big chances.
